rows.notes: Adds a group choice alternative; sockets (`$$name`) are extended the same way.
Resolved by checking every alternative; ambiguity is reported with `unique_choices` (#74).
In maps (including products of several choices, up to 1024 combinations) and in arrays.
On array entries, map members, groups and wildcard members (bounds and the default of exactly one are enforced, #151).

Members with bareword, text, integer (also negative), byte-string, bool, float and type keys; maps are closed unless a wildcard member allows more. A `null` (or `nil`) key written with `=>` is a required member like any other; `null: T` is the text key `"null"`.
A cut stops later wildcard members from claiming the key.
Entries are matched in order with backtracking, so an optional entry before another is fine (#135); lengths are checked (#133).

rows.notes: In maps and arrays, with occurrences, choices, sockets, recursion (also through arrays, #138) and generics (#72).
Splices the entries of a map or array into a map or array, and unwraps a tag as a type (#158). A map or array in a place that needs a type is a group, not a type, and matches nothing.
The choice of the values of a group's entries.
Instantiated where used (also in control arguments, #127); recursive generics terminate.
An empty socket matches nothing; extensions (`/=`, `//=`) from the schema and its modules are merged.
Self-referencing types, groups and generics; a rule defined only in terms of itself (`a = b`, `b = a`) is a schema error.
Includes dotted names such as `a.b`.
Syntax only: there is no data to reject. `0: tstr ; name` comments name fields in EDN (deprecation planned, #108).

Integer and float bounds, inclusive and exclusive; bounds of different kinds, or an empty range, are schema errors (#71).
Tag number and content are checked; nesting works. Tags are `(number, value)` tuples for now (#78).

rows.construct: Tag number given as a type `#6.<type>(t)`
rows.notes: Checked as the root rule, a map field, an array element and a choice alternative: the item must be a tag whose number matches `<type>` (`#6.<uint .le 10>(t)`, `#6.<1 / 2>(t)`) and whose content matches `t`. `#6(t)` accepts any tag. A bignum the decoder returns as an integer counts as tag 2 or 3.

`#M` matches data items of major type M, `#M.N` with N below 24 the value or length, `#7.20`-`#7.22` false, true and null, `#7.25`-`#7.27` any float, and `#` any item, as the root rule, field, element or choice alternative. The encoded width is not kept by the decoder, so `#0.26` is checked as `#0` (with a warning, #171), `#7.26` as any float (#169), and `#7.23` (undefined) and unassigned simple values match nothing because they cannot be decoded (#168).

rows.construct: Modules `;# import X as P`, `;# include X`
rows.notes: Draft comment syntax. Modules come from `modules=` / `--module` or a search path; one that is not found keeps its names unchecked and warns (#121). No RFC modules are bundled.

rows.construct: Integers (major types 0 and 1, up to 64 bits)
rows.notes: Non-shortest encodings are accepted by `loads()` (`1800` is 0); the optional deterministic check is #95.
Text strings must be valid UTF-8.
Duplicate map keys are rejected (#65); non-string keys keep their type (#88).
All three widths decode to a Python float; the encoder writes doubles unless `canonical=True` (shortest form that keeps the value). Width is lost on decoding (#169, #96).
Tags decode to `(number, value)` tuples, so a two-element tuple is ambiguous with a tag; a dedicated type is planned (#78). Bignums (2, 3) decode to Python ints in values.
